title: Pricing and Valuation of Interest Rates and Other Swaps
overview: A swap can be valued as offsetting cash-flow streams or as a series of forward contracts.
example: Write the payoff at expiration, build an equivalent position, and use no-arbitrage to compare values.

modules.title: Swap Valuation
modules.explanation: No-arbitrage valuation compares a derivative with a replicating portfolio that has the same future payoff. Carrying costs link spot and forward prices, swaps can be decomposed into forward cash flows, and options can be replicated across states.
steps: Write the derivative payoff at each relevant date or state.
Construct the equivalent position in the underlying, borrowing, lending, or simpler derivatives.
Set equal-payoff strategies to equal value and check signs, discounting, and exercise assumptions.

lesson: No-arbitrage valuation compares a derivative with a replicating portfolio that has the same future payoff. Carrying costs link spot and forward prices, swaps can be decomposed into forward cash flows, and options can be replicated across states.

Derivative analysis starts with the payoff and settlement terms, then uses replication or no-arbitrage to establish value. Because notional exposure can exceed invested cash, risk must be assessed from the full payoff rather than the initial payment.

For swap valuation, begin by asking what decision is being made and what evidence is available. Then follow the three-step method below. The final answer should state both the conclusion and the most important reason it may fail.
